rubrics.evidence: The patch removes the uniform `slugStage` interface entirely from pipeline.go (the whole twelve-method declaration including StageName, SubstituteCustoms, SubstituteLanguage, NormalizeASCII, ApplyCase, Truncate, ReplaceUnauthorized, CollapseDashes, TrimEdgeChars, SmartTruncate, AppendUniqueSuffix, and IsValidSlug is deleted). The shared `noopStage` carrier and all its pass-through method bodies are deleted. Every stage struct drops the `noopStage` embed: `languageSubstitutionStage`, `asciiNormalizationStage`, `caseFoldingStage`, `lengthGuardStage`, `sanitizingStage`, and `uniquifyingStage` all become `struct{}`. The hand-written pass-throughs on `customSubstitutionStage` (SubstituteLanguage, NormalizeASCII, ApplyCase, Truncate, ReplaceUnauthorized, CollapseDashes, TrimEdgeChars, SmartTruncate, AppendUniqueSuffix, IsValidSlug) are removed, leaving only SubstituteCustoms. `applyStages` now calls each phase directly on its owning stage (e.g. `text = custom.SubstituteCustoms(text)`, `text = language.SubstituteLanguage(text, lang)`) instead of routing every phase through every stage, and `IsSlug` inlines the validation logic rather than delegating to `noopStage{}.IsValidSlug`. No interface declaration remains that forces any participant to provide capabilities it does not own.
rubrics.criterion: After the patch, no interface declaration in the package forces a pipeline participant to provide text capabilities that the participant does not perform: the uniform contract that coupled the whole phase catalogue (substitutions, ASCII normalization, casing, both truncations, separator cleanup, timestamp suffix, plus the diagnostics and validation capabilities) onto every registered stage is gone, or is decomposed so that no participant satisfies capabilities it does not own through own or inherited pass-through method bodies.

rubrics.criterion: The slug generation entry point (the MakeLang path) is rewired to whatever structure replaces the pipeline participants, and it still performs the complete ordered phase sequence with the trim of the input, producing the pipeline phases in the same order as before the patch.

The phase order in applyStages (SubstituteCustoms, SubstituteLanguage, NormalizeASCII, ApplyCase, Truncate, ReplaceUnauthorized, CollapseDashes, TrimEdgeChars, SmartTruncate, AppendUniqueSuffix) matches the original sequence, preserving each option's effect.
rubrics.criterion: Every option-conditioned phase still consults its package option variable with the same effect as before the patch: casing follows Lowercase, the two truncation modes follow EnableSmartTruncate and MaxLength (both the word-boundary cut and the unconditional cut), dash collapsing follows DisableMultipleDashTrim, edge trimming follows DisableEndsTrim, and the suffix phase follows AppendTimestamp.

rubrics.evidence: In agent.patch, applyStages preserves the original phase order: custom.SubstituteCustoms -> language.SubstituteLanguage -> ascii.NormalizeASCII -> fold.ApplyCase -> length.Truncate -> sanitize.ReplaceUnauthorized -> sanitize.CollapseDashes -> sanitize.TrimEdgeChars -> length.SmartTruncate -> unique.AppendUniqueSuffix. customSubstitutionStage.SubstituteCustoms still applies runes before strings (SubstituteRune(s, CustomRuneSub) then Substitute(s, CustomSub)), ASCII normalization remains before unauthorized-symbol replacement, the timestamp suffix remains last, and the non-smart Truncate and SmartTruncate modes remain in their original positions. rubrics.criterion: The patch does not alter the ordering or content of the generation phases in a way that changes output, for example applying the string substitution map before the rune substitution map, running ASCII normalization after unauthorized-symbol replacement, truncating before all other phases run, applying the timestamp suffix before trimming and truncation, or swapping the two truncation modes.

rubrics.evidence: The patch preserves all phase behavior while removing the shared contract: applyStages still calls custom.SubstituteCustoms, language.SubstituteLanguage, ascii.NormalizeASCII, fold.ApplyCase, length.Truncate, sanitize.ReplaceUnauthorized, sanitize.CollapseDashes, sanitize.TrimEdgeChars, length.SmartTruncate, and unique.AppendUniqueSuffix. The implementing methods retain their original logic, e.g. lengthGuardStage.Truncate still does `if !EnableSmartTruncate && len(s) >= MaxLength { return s[:MaxLength] }`, sanitizingStage.CollapseDashes/TrimEdgeChars still honor DisableMultipleDashTrim/DisableEndsTrim, and uniquifyingStage.AppendUniqueSuffix still appends `"-" + timestamp()` when AppendTimestamp is set. No required phase was deleted with the contract machinery.
rubrics.criterion: The patch does not eliminate phase behavior in order to eliminate obligations, for example dropping the hard truncation performed when smart truncation is disabled, the dash collapsing, the edge trimming, the timestamp suffix, or the custom substitution pass, under the justification that the participant carrying it was part of the contract machinery.

rubrics.evidence: The patch preserves the package boundary contract: exported signatures are unchanged (MakeLang(s string, lang string) string still calls applyStages; IsSlug(text string) bool keeps its signature with the validation body restored inline), option variables (MaxLength, Lowercase, EnableSmartTruncate, DisableMultipleDashTrim, DisableEndsTrim, AppendTimestamp, CustomSub, CustomRuneSub) are referenced but never redeclared, and the word-boundary truncation helper remains a package-level function called with the same shape — lengthGuardStage.SmartTruncate calls smartTruncate(s), and timestamp() is likewise still a package-level function called by uniquifyingStage.AppendUniqueSuffix. No internal helper the tests bind to was restructured into a method or removed.
rubrics.criterion: The patch does not break the compilation contract around the package boundary: the exported functions keep their signatures, the option variables keep their names and types, and the internal helpers that the package's own benchmarks invoke directly (the word-boundary truncation helper in particular) remain callable as package-level functions with the same call shape.
